blocks.text: How do I find the gradient at a point on a curve?

blocks.md: - To find the gradient of a curve ***y*****= f(*****x*****)** at any point on the curve, substitute the ***x*****‑coordinate** of the point into the derivative **f'(*****x*****)**

blocks.alt: Grad Tang Norm Illustr 1, A Level & AS Maths: Pure revision notes

blocks.text: How do I find the equation of a tangent to a curve?

blocks.md: - At any point on a curve, the **tangent** is the line that goes through the point and has the same gradient as the curve at that point

blocks.alt: Grad Tang Norm Illustr 2, A Level & AS Maths: Pure revision notes

blocks.md: - For the curve y = f(x), you can find the equation of the **tangent** at the point (a, f(a)) using $y-f(a)=f^{'}(a)(x-a)$

blocks.text: How do I find the equation of a normal to a curve?

blocks.md: - At any point on a curve, the **normal** is the line that goes through the point and is **perpendicular** to the tangent at that point

blocks.alt: Grad Tang Norm Illustr 3, A Level & AS Maths: Pure revision notes

blocks.md: - For the curve y = f(x), you can find the equation of the **normal **at the point (a, f(a)) using $y-f(a)=-\frac{1}{f^{'}(a)}(x-a)$

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md: - The formulae above are not in the exam formulae booklet, but if you understand what tangents and normals are, then the formulae follow from the equation of a straight line combined with parallel and perpendicular gradients (see Worked Example below).
